title: Module Review Quiz: Exception Handling & Error Management

slides.title: Exception Handling Overview
slides.prompt: This Module Quiz covers try-catch blocks, throw statements, standard exceptions (std::exception), custom exception classes, exception safety guarantees, and noexcept specifier in C++ (CPP_241 to CPP_248).

slides.title: Try Block (CPP_241)
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword used to enclose a block of code that might throw an exception.

slides.title: Throw Statement (CPP_241)
slides.prompt: Which keyword is used to signal/raise an exception when an error condition occurs?

slides.title: Catch Block Syntax (CPP_242)
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword used to handle an exception thrown by a try block.

slides.title: Catch-All Handler (CPP_242)
slides.prompt: What syntax is used in a catch block parameter list to intercept any type of exception?

slides.title: Standard Exception Header (CPP_243)
slides.prompt: Fill in the standard header file name required to use base class std::exception and standard exceptions.

slides.title: std::exception Virtual Function (CPP_243)
slides.prompt: Which virtual member function of 'std::exception' returns an explanatory C-string describing the error?

slides.title: Custom Exception Class Inheritance (CPP_244)
slides.prompt: Fill in the standard exception class commonly derived to create custom runtime exceptions.

slides.title: noexcept Specifier (CPP_245)
slides.prompt: What does declaring a function with 'void process() noexcept;' indicate to the compiler?
options: The function guarantees it will not emit/throw any exceptions
The function throws exceptions automatically on failure
The function requires a try-catch block inside its body
The function cannot be called inside a loop
slides.correctAnswer: The function guarantees it will not emit/throw any exceptions

slides.title: noexcept Specifier Syntax (CPP_245)
slides.prompt: Fill in the specifier keyword guaranteeing zero exceptions from this cleanup method.

slides.title: Rethrowing Exceptions (CPP_246)
slides.prompt: How do you rethrow the currently caught exception object from inside a catch block?

slides.title: RAII Resource Management (CPP_247)
slides.prompt: Fill in the programming idiom (Acronym) where resource lifetime is tied to object lifetime to guarantee exception safety.
slides.codeSnippet:
// ___ principle prevents resource leaks during exceptions
std::unique_ptr<File> file;

slides.title: Uncaught Exceptions Behavior (CPP_248)
slides.prompt: What happens if an exception is thrown and no matching catch handler is found anywhere up the call stack?
options: std::terminate() is called and the program aborts immediately
The program ignores the exception and continues execution
The compiler automatically retries executing the function
The exception is converted into a compiler warning
slides.correctAnswer: std::terminate() is called and the program aborts immediately
